data.exact_reserve_text: While the information in the tables below provides a historical perspective on the adequacy of unpaid claims estimates established in previous years, readers of these financial statements are cautioned against extrapolating redundancies or deficiencies of the past on current unpaid loss provisions. The syndicate's management believes the estimated total claims provisions are adequate at the end of the current year.

prior_year_events.impact_description: The Ogden discount rate announcement on 27 February 2017 created an overnight profitability challenge for the Syndicate and the motor insurance industry, leading to reserve strengthening for the impact of the change in Ogden discount rates and deterioration on the forecast at year end 2016 due to reserve strengthening in damage losses.

data.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 218 experienced an overall gross prior year reserve release of GBP 29.643 million in 2017, representing a 4.16% reduction of its opening gross claims outstanding. This release was calculated from the gross claims development triangle. However, the report also highlights specific adverse developments, noting reserve strengthening due to the Ogden discount rate change announced in February 2017, which created profitability challenges for the motor insurance industry. There was also a deterioration on the 2016 year-end forecast due to reserve strengthening in damage losses and impacts from the Ogden rate change on unearned business. Other factors influencing claims severities and frequencies included the depreciation of the pound affecting imported parts and claimant behavior.
raw_causal_phrases: Ogden discount rate announcement on 27 February 2017. This discount rate change created an overnight profitability challenge for the Syndicate and the motor insurance industry.
This result includes reserve strengthening for the impact of the change in Ogden discount rates.

This forecast reflects a deterioration on the forecast at year end 2016 due to reserve strengthening in damage losses and the results of the unearned business at the year end which was impacted by the change in Ogden discount rates.
Ogden discount rate review: The possible future movement in the personal injury discount rate, also known as Ogden tables, from its current discount rate of minus 0.75% is a key uncertainty.
Propensities for Periodic Payment Orders (PPOs): The propensity for PPO payments will vary based upon the associated Ogden discount rate.

Further inflation in claim severities and frequencies: External factors could continue to increase claim severities, such as the depreciation of the pound affecting the prices of imported parts. Claimant behavior could also increase claim frequencies.
